position: end — after the verb or object

senses.gloss: In a polite, respectful way.
examples: The clerk *courteously* explained the return policy.
He *courteously* held the door for us.

senses.gloss: Secretly; without being seen or known.
examples: He glanced *covertly* at his phone under the table.

senses.gloss: With a strong wish to have something that belongs to someone else.
examples: He eyed his neighbor's new truck *covetously*.
The kids stared *covetously* at the candy display.
She looked *covetously* at the corner office.

senses.gloss: In a shy or playfully evasive way, often only pretending to be shy.
examples: The company *coyly* declined to name its new partner.
He *coyly* hinted that a sequel was coming.

senses.gloss: In a warm, comfortable, snug way.
examples: The cat was curled up *cozily* by the fire.

senses.gloss: In a clever, sly way meant to trick someone or gain an advantage.
examples: The fox *craftily* slipped past the dogs.
The rules were *craftily* written to favor insiders.

modifies: verbs; adjectives in the degree sense

senses.gloss: In a wild, uncontrolled way.
examples: The car swerved *crazily* across the lanes.
The dog ran *crazily* around the yard.

senses.gloss: Extremely; to an unreasonable degree (informal).
examples: Rents in this city are *crazily* high.

senses.gloss: In an original, imaginative way.
examples: Teachers have to think *creatively* with small budgets.
The team solved the problem more *creatively* than we expected.

senses.gloss: In a way that can be believed or trusted.
examples: No one could *credibly* claim the vote was rigged.
The witness spoke *credibly* about what she saw.
He has been *credibly* accused of fraud.

senses.gloss: Under criminal law.
examples: The company could be held *criminally* liable.
Only one of the executives was charged *criminally*.

senses.gloss: Shamefully; to an outrageous degree (informal).
examples: The actress is *criminally* underused in the film.

senses.gloss: In a clean, sharp, brisk way.
By judging carefully, looking for faults as well as strengths.
examples: Students need to think *critically* about their sources.

senses.gloss: So seriously that life is in danger.
examples: Two people were *critically* injured in the crash.

senses.gloss: Extremely; at a decisive level.
examples: Clean water is *critically* important after a flood.
Blood supplies are *critically* low this month.

senses.gloss: At an angle; not straight.
examples: The picture hung *crookedly* on the wall.
Her glasses sat *crookedly* on her nose.

ru: через всю страну; по пересечённой местности
form: compound — also an adjective (*a cross-country race*)

senses.gloss: Across a whole country, especially from one coast to the other.
examples: They flew *cross-country* to see her parents.

senses.gloss: Across fields and open land rather than along roads.
With the legs crossed, especially sitting on the floor with the knees apart.
examples: The kids sat *cross-legged* on the rug.
She sat *cross-legged* on the bed, reading.
He was sitting *cross-legged* in front of the TV.

form: compound — also an adjective (*a crosstown bus*)

senses.gloss: Across a city, from one side to the other.
examples: We took a cab *crosstown* to the theater.
She moved *crosstown* to be closer to her office.

senses.gloss: Across; at a right angle to the length of something.
examples: Slice the carrots *crosswise* into thin rounds.
Lay the boards *crosswise* over the ditch.

modifies: a whole clause; adjectives and verbs (*crucially important*, *depends crucially*)

senses.gloss: Most importantly; used to point out the key fact.
examples: *Crucially*, the test was done before the drug was approved.
The plan is cheap and, *crucially*, fast.

senses.gloss: In a decisive way; to a very great degree.
examples: The outcome depends *crucially* on the weather.

senses.gloss: In a rough, simple way, without skill or detail.
examples: The sign was *crudely* painted on a board.
The shelter was *crudely* built from branches.
To put it *crudely*, they just want your money.

senses.gloss: In a vulgar, offensive way.
In a way that causes pain or suffering, on purpose or with painful unfairness.
examples: Her career was *cruelly* cut short by injury.

senses.gloss: Overwhelmingly; to a crushing degree.
In a mysterious way that is hard to understand.
examples: The note was signed *cryptically* with a single letter.

senses.gloss: Taken together; by adding up over time.
examples: The effects of lost sleep build up *cumulatively*.
Small changes can *cumulatively* make a big difference.

senses.gloss: In a sly, deceptive way.
examples: He *cunningly* hid the losses from investors.
She *cunningly* played the two rivals against each other.

senses.gloss: Cleverly and skillfully.
examples: The drawer is *cunningly* hidden in the desk.

senses.gloss: Quickly and without attention to detail.
examples: He glanced *cursorily* at the contract and signed it.
The inspector looked *cursorily* around the kitchen.

senses.gloss: In a rudely short way.
examples: The email *curtly* informed him that his contract was over.

senses.gloss: As is usual or traditional.
examples: The bride's family *customarily* pays for the wedding.
The award is *customarily* presented in the spring.

senses.gloss: In a way that assumes the worst about people's motives, or that exploits others without caring.
examples: Some voters *cynically* assume all politicians lie.
He smiled *cynically* when she mentioned loyalty.

senses.gloss: In a small, delicate, graceful way.
examples: The cat stepped *daintily* over the puddle.
He *daintily* dabbed his mouth with a napkin.

form: flat — the same form as the adjective *damn*
contrast: Informal and mildly offensive; keep it out of formal writing. *Damn well* adds force to a verb (*You know damn well*). *Darn* is the softer version.

senses.gloss: Very; extremely (informal).
examples: You know *damn* well what I mean.

modifies: verbs, adjectives and adverbs (*dangerously low*, *dangerously fast*)

senses.gloss: In a way that could cause harm or put someone at risk.
examples: The patient's blood pressure was *dangerously* low.
The crowd surged *dangerously* toward the stage.

senses.gloss: Boldly; in a way that takes risks.
examples: The climber *daringly* scaled the cliff without ropes.

senses.gloss: In a gloomy, threatening, or mysterious way.
With a dark color or little light.
In a stylish, confident, attractive way.
examples: He looked *dashingly* handsome in his uniform.
The actor was *dashingly* dressed in a white suit.
The hero rode *dashingly* to the rescue.

senses.gloss: In a way that seems hard or big enough to discourage you.
examples: The math behind the model is *dauntingly* complex.
Her calendar for the week looked *dauntingly* full.

senses.gloss: So brightly or impressively that it dazzles.
examples: The lake sparkled *dazzlingly* in the sun.

form: flat — the same form as the adjective *deadly*
contrast: Usually an adjective (*a deadly virus*). As an adverb it only intensifies a few words: *deadly serious* means *completely serious*, not *dangerously serious*.

senses.gloss: Extremely; completely.

form: flat — the same form as the adjective *deathly*

senses.gloss: Extremely, in a way that suggests death.
In a dishonest way meant to trick people.
examples: The company acted *deceitfully* toward its customers.
She was *deceitfully* lured into the scheme.

senses.gloss: In a proper, respectable, or fair way.
Fairly well; well enough.

contrast: *Deceptively simple* means it only looks simple and is really hard. With some adjectives the meaning is unclear (*deceptively large* — bigger or smaller than it looks?), so careful writers avoid those.

senses.gloss: In a way that gives a false impression.
examples: The current is *deceptively* strong near the shore.
The drink was *deceptively* labeled as juice.

contrast: *Decidedly* means *clearly, definitely* (*decidedly colder*). *Decisively* means *firmly, without hesitating* or *by a clear margin* (*act decisively*, *win decisively*).

senses.gloss: Clearly; without doubt.
examples: The mood in the room was *decidedly* hostile.
Her new album is *decidedly* better than the last one.

senses.gloss: Quickly and firmly, without hesitating.
examples: The governor acted *decisively* to stop the outbreak.

senses.gloss: In a way that settles something clearly.
In a way that reacts to criticism as if under attack.
examples: 'I was only trying to help,' he said *defensively*.

senses.gloss: So as to protect against attack, as in sports, war or driving.
With polite respect for someone's rank or opinion.
examples: The staff spoke *deferentially* to the senator.
Reporters treated the coach far too *deferentially*.

senses.gloss: In a way that openly refuses to obey or give in.
examples: The protesters stayed *defiantly* in the square.

senses.gloss: Quickly and skillfully.
In a sad, discouraged way.
examples: She sighed *dejectedly* and closed her laptop.
The fans sat *dejectedly* in the rain.

comparison: more/most — mainly in the second sense

senses.gloss: On purpose.
examples: He *deliberately* left out the bad news.

senses.gloss: Slowly and carefully.
Carefully and tactfully, so as not to offend or damage anything.
examples: She *delicately* raised the subject of money.

senses.gloss: In a fine, light, or subtle way.
examples: The soup is *delicately* flavored with ginger.
The vase is *delicately* painted with birds.

senses.gloss: In a way that tastes or smells very good.
Very pleasantly; in a way that is great fun.
With great pleasure.
examples: She clapped *delightedly* when she saw the cake.

contrast: *Delightfully* describes what gives pleasure (*a delightfully quiet hotel*); *delightedly* describes a person who feels it (*she clapped delightedly*).

senses.gloss: In a way that gives great pleasure.
Extremely, with wild excitement.
In a confused state caused by fever or illness.
examples: She talked *deliriously* while the fever lasted.

senses.gloss: By voting or in a way that gives everyone an equal say.
examples: It was the country's first *democratically* chosen government.

senses.gloss: In a way that can be clearly shown or proved.
examples: Schools that tried it saw *demonstrably* better results.

senses.gloss: In a quiet, modest, reserved way.
examples: The children sat *demurely* in the front pew.
She was *demurely* dressed in a long gray skirt.

senses.gloss: With parts or people crowded closely together.
examples: The book is *densely* packed with footnotes.

senses.gloss: In a way you can rely on.
examples: She has *dependably* shown up early for ten years.

senses.gloss: In a shockingly bad way that deserves strong criticism.
examples: The animals were kept in *deplorably* dirty cages.
Staffing at the hospital is *deplorably* low.

modifies: adjectives and adverbs; a whole clause at the front

senses.gloss: In a way that makes you feel sad or hopeless.
In a mocking way that shows contempt.
examples: Critics *derisively* called the stadium 'the money pit.'

modifies: verbs, adjectives, or a whole clause (*and deservedly so*)

senses.gloss: As someone or something deserves; rightly.
examples: She is *deservedly* proud of her work.
The restaurant is popular, and *deservedly* so.

senses.gloss: In a way that shows you have lost all hope.
examples: 'What do we do now?' she asked *despairingly*.
They looked *despairingly* at the flooded basement.

senses.gloss: With despair, trying anything because the situation is so bad.
examples: She searched *desperately* for a way out.

senses.gloss: Extremely; very much.
examples: The town *desperately* needs a new hospital.

senses.gloss: In a morally shameful way that deserves contempt.
examples: Treating a child that way is *despicably* cruel.

senses.gloss: In a sad, hopeless, discouraged way.
examples: He stared *despondently* at the rejection letter.
The players trudged *despondently* to the locker room.

senses.gloss: In a way that causes damage or harm.
examples: The storm moved *destructively* along the coast.

senses.gloss: With firm purpose; refusing to give up.
examples: The toddler marched *determinedly* toward the cookies.

senses.gloss: In a harmful way (formal).
examples: The new rules may *detrimentally* impact small businesses.
Too much screen time can affect sleep *detrimentally*.

senses.gloss: In terms of a child's physical or mental growth.
examples: The toys are *developmentally* appropriate for toddlers.
*Developmentally*, twins usually catch up by age two.

senses.gloss: Very; extremely.
In a sneaky, dishonest way.
examples: He *deviously* shifted the blame to his partner.
She smiled *deviously* as she dealt the cards.

senses.gloss: With loyal love and care.
examples: Fans have *devotedly* watched the show for twenty years.

senses.gloss: In a deeply religious way.
Sincerely; very much, with *hope* or *wish*.
examples: I *devoutly* hope this is the last meeting.
It's an outcome we should all *devoutly* wish for.

senses.gloss: With skillful use of the hands or mind.
In an extremely wicked or fiendishly clever way.
In a slanting line from one corner to the opposite one.
examples: The bank is *diagonally* across from the post office.

senses.gloss: Completely, as far apart as possible.
examples: The two plans go in *diametrically* opposite directions.
She and her father hold *diametrically* opposed opinions.

contrast: Standard English uses *differently* after a verb; *think different* is a slogan, not correct grammar. Americans usually say *differently than* (*she acts differently than her sister*); *differently from* is also correct.

senses.gloss: In another way; not in the same way.
Shyly, without confidence.
examples: She knocked *diffidently* on the office door.
'Maybe we could try again?' he asked *diffidently*.

senses.gloss: By means of computers or digital technology.
examples: The old films have been *digitally* restored.

senses.gloss: With steady, careful effort.
examples: She studied *diligently* for the bar exam.

position: before its word; also mid or end
modifies: participles, adjectives and verbs (*dimly lit*, *dimly aware*)

senses.gloss: With little light.
examples: A lamp glowed *dimly* in the window.

senses.gloss: Vaguely; not clearly.
examples: I *dimly* remember the house we lived in.
She was *dimly* aware of someone calling her name.

senses.gloss: Tactfully, so as not to upset anyone.
Through diplomacy between countries.
In an unpleasant or bad-tempered way.
In a way that shows you feel let down.

modifies: adjectives and adverbs; a whole clause at the front
contrast: *Disappointingly* describes the thing that lets you down (*disappointingly slow*); *disappointedly* describes how a person feels (*she sighed disappointedly*).

senses.gloss: In a way that falls short of what was hoped for.
In a way that shows you think something is wrong or bad.
examples: The librarian looked *disapprovingly* over her glasses.

senses.gloss: In a way that causes a disaster or turns out very badly.
examples: The team played *disastrously* in the second half.

senses.gloss: In a way that shows you cannot believe something.
examples: She stared *disbelievingly* at the lottery ticket.

modifies: adjectives; a whole clause at the front

senses.gloss: In a way that makes you uneasy or confused.
Very sadly, in a way nothing can comfort.
examples: The boy sat *disconsolately* on the curb.
She wandered *disconsolately* through the empty house.
The fans stared *disconsolately* at the scoreboard.

modifies: adjectives and adverbs; a whole clause at the front

senses.gloss: In a way that makes you lose hope or confidence.
examples: The early test results were *discouragingly* bad.

contrast: Sounds exactly like *discretely* (*separately, as distinct parts*), a different and much rarer word.

senses.gloss: Quietly and carefully, so as not to attract attention or cause embarrassment.
examples: He coughed *discreetly* to get their attention.

senses.gloss: In a way that shows you think something is not worth your respect.
examples: She looked *disdainfully* at the cheap wine.
The critic wrote *disdainfully* about pop music.

senses.gloss: In a shamefully bad way.
In a way that shows strong dislike or disgust.
examples: He tossed the moldy bread away *disgustedly*.

contrast: *Disgustingly* describes the thing that disgusts (*disgustingly dirty*); *disgustedly* describes how a person reacts (*she said disgustedly*).

senses.gloss: In a way that causes disgust.
examples: He chewed *disgustingly* with his mouth open.

senses.gloss: To an annoying or enviable degree (informal, often joking).
examples: She's always *disgustingly* cheerful in the morning.

senses.gloss: In a way that lies, cheats, or deceives.
examples: The ad *dishonestly* suggests the pills cure cancer.

senses.gloss: In a way that brings shame or breaks a moral code.
examples: He was *dishonorably* discharged from the Army.
They acted *dishonorably* in breaking the deal.

senses.gloss: Insincerely, pretending to be innocent or to know less than you do.
examples: He *disingenuously* claimed he'd never seen the memo.
The company *disingenuously* called the layoffs a 'restructuring.'
She asked, a little *disingenuously*, what all the fuss was about.
